title: Josephson effect in symmetry-mismatched van der Waals hybrid junctions of NbSe2-Bi2Sr2CaCu2O8+x and NbSe2-Bi2Sr2-xLaxCuO6+y
authors: Yuying Zhu, Ziye Liu, Hongtao Yan, Lin Zhao, Xingjiang Zhou, Qi-Kun Xue, Ding Zhang
abstract: Coupling superconductors of different symmetries may lead to emergent quantum phenomena but experimental studies on heterojunctions made of lattice-mismatched crystals are scarce. Here, we fabricate Josephson junction by van der Waals stacking NbSe2 flakes on freshly cleaved surfaces of Bi2Sr2CaCu2O8+x or Bi2Sr2-xLaxCuO6+y. We obtain pronounced Josephson currents across the heterojunctions at temperatures below 7 K. The Josephson coupling strength, characterized by the product of the critical Josephson current I_c and the normal state resistance R_n, can reach about 0.3 mV, much exceeding the values previously reported in Pb-Bi2Sr2CaCu2O8+x or Nb-Bi2Sr2CaCu2O8+x junctions. Microwave irradiation induces integer Shapiro steps. We also observe the Fraunhofer diffraction pattern by applying an in-plane magnetic field. We compare our results with the theoretical calculations that take into account the coherent tunneling and the order parameter mixing. Our work demonstrates the hybrid junctions as a distinctive platform for addressing pairing symmetry and emergent quantum phenomena.
summary: This work reports on the creation and characterization of novel Josephson junctions using van der Waals stacking of $	ext{NbSe}_2$ onto cuprate superconductors. By measuring critical currents, observing Shapiro steps, and analyzing magnetic responses, the authors demonstrate a high-quality platform for studying the interplay between different superconducting symmetries. This advances the understanding of interfacial quantum phenomena in high-temperature superconductors.
main_problem: Investigating the Josephson effect and emergent quantum phenomena in hybrid junctions formed by van der Waals stacking of $	ext{NbSe}_2$ onto cuprate superconductors ($	ext{Bi2212}$/$	ext{Bi2201}$).
main_result: The study successfully observed pronounced Josephson currents ($I_c R_n \sim 0.3 	ext{ mV}$) and confirmed the Josephson effect via Shapiro steps, establishing these junctions as a platform to study pairing symmetry.
method: The research combines experimental transport measurements (I-V curves, magnetic field dependence) with theoretical modeling of Josephson coupling strength.
model_or_system: The physical system is a Josephson junction formed by van der Waals stacking of $	ext{NbSe}_2$ (a conventional superconductor) onto high-temperature cuprate superconductors ($	ext{Bi2Sr2CaCu2O}_{8+x}$ or $	ext{Bi2Sr}_{2-x}	ext{La}_x	ext{CuO}_{6+y}$).
key_observables: Josephson critical current ($I_c$), Josephson coupling strength ($I_c R_n$), Shapiro steps, and Fraunhofer diffraction pattern.
important_parameters: Temperature (below 7 K), junction area, and superconducting pairing symmetries (e.g., $s$-wave vs. $d$-wave).
main_assumptions: The theoretical analysis compares results with models considering coherent tunneling and order parameter mixing, though limitations exist in determining precise geometric parameters like twist angles.
figures_summary: Figures show the stacking process, temperature dependence of resistance, $I-V$ characteristics exhibiting Shapiro steps under microwave irradiation, and Fraunhofer diffraction patterns under in-plane magnetic fields.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by fabricating the junctions, measuring transport properties (I-V, magnetic response), confirming the Josephson effect, and comparing these experimental findings with theoretical calculations that account for superconducting order parameter mixing.
why_interesting: The study directly probes superconducting pairing symmetries (e.g., $d$-wave nature of cuprates) at an interface, which is a key area of research in strongly correlated electron systems, and uses advanced junction physics to probe these symmetries.
